source.title: Surgical Refusal Ablation: Disentangling Safety from Intelligence via Concept-Guided Spectral Cleaning

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the idea that a refusal direction can be polysemantic to motivate a cleaning method. Its measurements concern refusal vectors and their ablation, not individual neurons or the behaviors named in V1–V7.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about contrastive refusal directions, including overlaps with capability/style directions and outcomes after ablating standard or cleaned refusal directions. These are related to, but do not measure, the neuron-level claims in the listed versions; rows are therefore linked to none. The figure-only concept maps and spectral plots are not transcribed as numerical rows. No results from cited work are included.
record.test_reason: The paper borrows the word 'polysemantic' for a contrastive refusal direction in the residual stream, not for individual neurons. It reports refusal rates, perplexity and KL after its own ablation method versus standard ablation. No neuron's response to unrelated inputs is measured, so none of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that the raw refusal vector entangles refusal with capability and style directions. Removing those components (SRA) gives deep refusal reduction with much less drift, so much ablation 'damage' is an artifact of an imprecise direction.
record.recipe_differences: The study cleans a contrastive refusal direction using a curated registry of capability/style atoms, then applies rank-one weight updates; the listed original sources concern neuron/circuit interpretation and Softmax Linear Units, not this refusal-direction cleaning procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by model: standard ablation leaves 42.0% refusal on Qwen3-VL-8B and 12.0% on Ministral-14B, while SRA reports 2.0% and 0.0%, respectively. Standard-ablation drift also varies substantially across models.

fits_no_version.finding: The contrastive refusal direction has non-trivial cosine with capability atoms (Logic ≈ −0.22, Coding ≈ +0.18 in Qwen3-VL-2B). The authors call such a direction 'polysemantic'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrastive mean-difference steering directions mix the target behaviour with capability and style directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Residualizing the refusal direction against capability/style atoms before ablation keeps refusal reduction (0–2%) while cutting WT2 perplexity change and first-token KL relative to standard ablation. GSM8K and MBPP perplexity is roughly preserved.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cleaning a refusal direction of entangled components reduces collateral drift from refusal ablation.

record.problems: The paper notes that its atom registry is curated and may miss confounds, the harmful prompt suite is finite, refusal detection depends on its definition, and perplexity and first-token KL are proxies rather than comprehensive downstream evaluations. No error bars, confidence intervals, or p-values are reported in the presented tables. The findings concern refusal directions and do not directly establish neuron-level polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted to meet the row limit. Figure-only concept maps and spectral-component plots are not recorded as rows because their values are not given in text or tables.

untested.parts: No vision models or neurons are studied.
No MLP neuron responses to tokens or contexts are measured.
Superposition and capacity are not examined at neuron level. Direction entanglement is only hypothesised (Eq. 2).
Initialization, regularization and training-noise causes are not studied.
Neuron polysemanticity is not compared across architectures or activation functions.
Canonical polysemantic neurons are not re-examined.
Activation ranges and explanation-scoring methods are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: Here 'polysemantic' refers to residual-stream steering vectors, not neurons, so the study is off-topic for this phenomenon. The row states (observed/partial) were assigned against no version and carry no claim meaning. Other weaknesses: a single author, a preprint, no uncertainty reported, and the concept maps are given only as figures.

versions.untested_parts: No image-classifier neurons or individual neuron responses are studied.
No transformer MLP neurons are measured for responses to tokens or contexts.
No neuron-level superposition or feature-to-neuron capacity pressure is tested.
Initialization, regularization, training noise, and neuron-level polysemanticity with spare capacity are not tested.
No neuron-level polysemanticity rates are compared across activation functions, architectures, or regularization settings.
The paper studies refusal directions rather than canonical polysemantic neurons or shared features in those neurons.
The paper does not vary neuron activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods.

relation.reason: The term and idea are used for a steering direction, and nothing tests neuron polysemanticity. 'discusses' is arguable, since the paper cites no polysemantic-neuron literature, but uses_without_test is acceptable.

tranche.reason: Borrows polysemanticity as the motivating idea for a residual-stream refusal direction and reports only its own ablation method's refusal, perplexity and KL results. It measures no neuron-level polysemanticity.

source_check.notes: The cosines come from one illustrative Introduction sentence, with no layer, baseline or null. The Section 4.1 heatmap (layers 15-25) gives no numbers in the text. This is not neuron-level evidence for any of V1-V7.

statements.correction: Qwen3-VL-2B: the raw (dirty) refusal direction has cosine about -0.22 with the Logic atom and about +0.18 with the Coding atom (Introduction). The authors call it polysemantic; it is a residual-stream direction, not a neuron.
statements.problem: none. The text says the raw contrastive refusal vector is 'polysemantic', with non-trivial cosine to the Logic (about -0.22) and Coding (about +0.18) atoms in Qwen3-VL-2B. It is a residual-stream steering direction, not a neuron.
